vt32_what_survived.topic: Parallels outside Christianity: the Sufi al-Hallaj's execution in Baghdad, 922

claims.text: Al-Hallaj, Persian Sufi, born c.858, died 26 March 922 in Baghdad.

Al-Hallaj was condemned in 922 and executed on the banks of the Tigris; Caliph al-Muqtadir first revoked the order, then approved it under the vizier's pressure; the charge presented him as a Qarmatian rebel wishing to destroy the Kaaba, citing his saying that what matters is to go seven times around 'the Kaaba of one's heart'; Ernst: heresy was treated as a political crime. 'Ana al-Haqq' ('I am the Truth') is read by some as a claim to divinity, by others as annihilation of the ego; its link to his execution owes much to Attar's later biography.

vt32_obligation.topic: Tithe made compulsory by the Frankish state (Herstal 779) and the Sunday obligation today (CCC 2180-2181, canon 1247)

claims.text: Capitulary of Herstal, drawn up March 779 (Mordek; Boretius favoured 780, Ganshof 792-793): tithe payment 'is made obligatory throughout the Frankish kingdom', with part set aside for the poor, after the crises of 778.

CCC 2180 quotes canon 1247: 'On Sundays and other holy days of obligation the faithful are bound to participate in the Mass'; CCC 2181: the Sunday Eucharist is 'the foundation and confirmation of all Christian practice'; excused for serious reason (illness, care of infants) or dispensation; 'Those who deliberately fail in this obligation commit a grave sin.'
